data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical immunomodulators & antipsoriatics_

**Class:** Topical immunotherapy with strong contact allergens — diphenylcyclopropenone (DPCP), dinitrochlorobenzene (DNCB), squaric acid dibutyl ester (SADBE)

## Mechanism of action
- Induce allergic contact dermatitis (type IV) at the site → 'antigenic competition': recruits suppressor T cells and cytokines that disrupt the autoimmune attack on hair follicles or the immune evasion of HPV
- DNCB is mutagenic (Ames test) — largely abandoned; DPCP and SADBE are preferred

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Extensive or chronic alopecia areata (DPCP — the most studied; response 30–60%)
- Recalcitrant viral warts, multiple warts in children (SADBE/DPCP)

## Dose & formulations
- Sensitise with 2% DPCP to a small area (arm/scalp patch); after 2 weeks apply weekly starting at 0.001%, increasing concentration until a mild eczematous reaction (itch and erythema lasting 24–36 h) is achieved; leave 48 h, shield from light (DPCP is light-degraded)
- Regrowth after 8–12 weeks; continue for at least 6 months before calling failure
- Wear gloves; store in amber bottles

## Adverse effects
- Severe eczema, blistering, regional lymphadenopathy
- Pigmentary changes — dyschromia in confetti pattern, vitiligo (especially dark skin)
- Urticaria, erythema multiforme-like reactions; sensitisation of staff (gloves)

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy and women planning pregnancy; DNCB (mutagenic) — not recommended

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated (DPCP not studied; DNCB mutagenic).

## Viva points
- Antigenic competition mechanism
- DNCB mutagenic → DPCP preferred
- Shield DPCP from light; titrate to mild dermatitis

_Sources: Khopkar ch.23 (DNCB, DPCP, SADBE); Wolverton 4e ch.57. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
